# Why is the translation block of Pinocchio's floating base Jcom not the identity matrix, and how can it be aligned with MuJoCo's local coordinate result?

> **Current answer:** The maintainer identified the primary cause as the coordinate system: the Pinocchio center-of-mass Jacobian expressed in world coordinates, while the original post's MuJoCo data was interpreted in the waist local coordinate system. The maintainer suggested using data.oMi[1].rotation.T * Jc to rotate the Pinocchio result into local coordinates; the author tested and reported a significant reduction in error. Therefore, one cannot directly compare the first three columns with the identity matrix; the target coordinate system and correct joint ID must be clarified.

## Key terms

- Center-of-mass Jacobian (Jcom) (质心雅可比)
- World frame (世界坐标系)
- Local frame (局部坐标系)
- FreeFlyer (自由浮动基)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why are the first three columns of the floating base Jcom not the identity matrix, and are the Pinocchio and MuJoCo Jcom/matrix values different?
- What coordinate system and action point correspond to Pinocchio's WORLD, LOCAL Jacobian, and data.v[id]?
- When using non-unit base pose, the translation block of Pinocchio Jcom shows ~1e-2 non-diagonal elements, while the user expected an identity matrix.
- The quality matrix on both sides is consistent under fixed base, but becomes significantly different after adding FreeFlyer and rotating the base non-unit.

## Environment

- Pinocchio 2018 Python/C++, MuJoCo comparison; user provided minimal URDF with floating joints, two-legged URDF state, and full matrix output; specific release version not mentioned.

## Priority diagnostics

- First determine the coordinate system and action point of the Jacobian being compared; rotate Pinocchio's world Jcom to the target local coordinate system before comparison.
- Compare using unit base rotation and non-unit rotation to confirm differences are due to floating base representation.
- Cross-validate quality matrix using RNEA and appropriate reference frame, rather than comparing individual elements of two libraries' raw matrices.

## Possible causes

- Pinocchio Jcom expressed in world coordinates, while the user's MuJoCo data was interpreted in the waist local coordinate system.
- Pinocchio's floating base velocity, acceleration, and force components are expressed in first body coordinates, while MuJoCo's comparison matrix is in world coordinates.

## Attempts

- The maintainer provided data.oMi[1].rotation.T * Jc for comparison; the author applied the rotation and reported a significant reduction in error.
- The author compared fixed base and FreeFlyer, setting both base poses to unit; under unit pose, matrix error reduced to ~1e-8 to 1e-10.

## Effective fixes

- Compare Jcom before converting both sides to the same coordinate system; the original thread used data.oMi[1].rotation.T for the first floating rigid body.
- Read joint local velocity by first forwardKinematics(model, data, q, qdot), then use data.v[id]; only change coordinate system by rotating linear/angular components, not the action point.

## Result

- The author confirmed reduced error after Jcom rotation and confirmed WORLD/LOCAL explanation is clear.
- The author obtained nearly identical quality matrices on both sides under unit base rotation, and attributed remaining non-unit rotation difference to floating base representation.

## Limitations

- Original thread did not provide a general MuJoCo↔Pinocchio quality matrix basis transformation formula, nor closed all bias term differences completely.
- data.oMi[1] is only suitable for the first target joint in this minimal model; actual system requires correct joint ID.
